operations.summary: Retrieves a user's coding-time summary for all time since today. Set `user` to a user ID or `current` to select the user whose summary you want.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User ID to fetch data for (or 'current')

operations.summary: Retrieves badge data for a user, interval, and filter in a format compatible with Shields.io. Use `interval` to choose the aggregation period and `filter` to select an entity such as a project or language; public data access must be enabled for the user.
operations.description: Retrieve total time for a given entity (e.g. a project) within a given range (e.g. one week) in a format compatible with [Shields.io](https://shields.io/endpoint). Requires public data access to be allowed.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User ID to fetch data for

operations.summary: Retrieves the application's health status. Use this endpoint to check the service's current health without supplying request parameters or a body.
Lists a user's heartbeats for a specified date. Provide `date` to select the day and `user` to identify whose activity to retrieve.

Retrieves a summary of activity for the requested interval or date range. Use `from` and `to` to define the period, and apply project, language, editor, operating system, machine, or label filters to narrow the summary.

parameters.name: recompute
parameters.description: Whether to recompute the summary from raw heartbeat or use cache

operations.summary: Lists users ranked by coding activity in descending order. Use this endpoint to retrieve the leaderboard, including its ranking data, current-user information, and range metadata.
Retrieves a single project for a specified user. Provide `user` to select the user and `id` to identify the project.
operations.description: Mimics undocumented endpoint related to https://wakatime.com/developers#projects

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User ID to fetch data for (or 'current')

operations.summary: Lists a user's projects. Set `user` to a user ID or `current`, and optionally use `q` to filter the projects.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User ID to fetch data for (or 'current')

operations.summary: Retrieves coding-activity statistics for a user over a selected interval. Use the optional query parameters to filter the statistics by project, language, editor, operating system, machine, or project label.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User ID to fetch data for (or 'current')

operations.summary: Retrieves WakaTime-compatible summaries for a specified user. Use `range` or the `start` and `end` dates to select a period, and apply project, language, editor, operating system, machine, or label filters to narrow the results.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User ID to fetch data for (or 'current')

operations.summary: Retrieves a user's profile information. Set `user` to a user ID or `current` to retrieve the profile associated with the authenticated user.
Lists the unique user agents recorded for a specified user. Use the `user` path parameter to select the user whose agent history you want to inspect.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User ID to fetch data for (or 'current')

operations.summary: Submits a diagnostics object sent by the WakaTime CLI. Include diagnostic details such as the CLI version, platform, logs, or stack trace to provide context for the reported issue.
Submits a single heartbeat containing activity data. Send the heartbeat as a JSON object, using fields such as `entity`, `category`, and `language` to describe the recorded activity.

Creates a heartbeat for the specified user. Submit a JSON object with the activity data you want to record, such as `entity`, `language`, `category`, and line-change values. The schema does not mark any heartbeat fields as required.
Creates a single heartbeat for a user from a WakaTime-compatible request. Send the heartbeat as a JSON object; `created_at` is numeric, and the `editor` field is ignored.
Submits a single heartbeat for a specified user. Send the heartbeat as a JSON object containing activity data such as `entity`, `category`, and `language`.
Submits multiple heartbeats in one request. Send a JSON array of heartbeat objects to record activity in bulk.

Creates multiple heartbeats for the specified user. Submit a JSON array of heartbeat objects containing the activity data you want to record. The schema does not mark any fields within the heartbeat objects as required.
Creates multiple heartbeats for a user from a WakaTime-compatible request. Send a JSON array of heartbeat objects; each object can include fields such as `entity`, `language`, and `created_at`.
Submits multiple heartbeats for a specified user in one request. Send a JSON array of heartbeat objects to record activity in bulk.
Retrieves today's activity summary for a specified user in a status-bar-compatible format. Use the `user` path parameter to select the user whose current-day activity you want to view.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User ID to fetch data for (or 'current')

properties.name: projects
properties.description: Previously, all the following properties created a cascade foreign key constraint on the summary_items table back to this summary table resulting in 5 identical foreign key constraints on the summary_items table. This is not a problem for PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite, but for MSSQL (not supported anymore though), which complains about circular cascades on update/delete between these two tables. All of these created foreign key constraints are identical, so only one constraint is enough. MySQL will create a foreign key constraint for every property referencing other structs, even no constraint is specified in tags. So explicitly set gorm:"-" in all other properties to avoid creating duplicate foreign key constraints
